Example Campaign Family, a campaign family that uses fake job interviews

Also seen as: ECF

A campaign family that reaches developers through fake job offers and delivers malware through meeting apps, coding tests, packages and terminal commands.

First seen
2026-08-15
Last seen
2026-10-31
Delivery
Fake meeting app, Coding test repository, npm package, Terminal command
Targeted systems
Windows, macOS, Linux

What it steals

  • Browser passwords
  • Crypto wallet files
  • Session cookies

Attribution

  • Linked to the fictional Fixture Group, as stated by Fake meeting apps that target job seekers (Vendor Example Research, 2026-10-20)
  • Shares its installer code, build J3qMXicxfX4H5at1w0ef9IDynYtyoWF29zgeh6NZ4xGBA2TXCeO48mOt71EBhZJk, with an earlier fixture campaign, as stated by Installer code shared between two fixture campaigns (Second Vendor Example, 2026-10-27)

Names this family used

  • Example Front Company Front 2026-11-02
  • Avery Exampleton (name used by the campaign, possibly a stolen identity) Front 2026-11-01
  • Example Source Only App Front 2026-10-31
  • Riley Placeholder (name used by the campaign, possibly a stolen identity) Front 2026-10-20

What happened

The cited sources describe the family as using several delivery routes at once.
